Senses.Explanation: A dry shit-stick is the latrine wiping-tool named by the compound. Linji Yixuan asks what dry shit-stick the person of no rank is; Deshan Xuanjian predicates it of old Shakyamuni; and Yunmen Wenyan asks what dry shit-stick an assembly seeks to chew. In Yunmen’s famous case it answers ‘What is Buddha?’ Wumen Huikai preserves Yunmen as the answerer, Dahui Zonggao repeats the case in verse, and Zhongfeng Mingben places it beside the courtyard cypress and three catties of hemp as sayings with no route for explanatory boring. Wanpu Zhao later asks Miyun Yuanwu what it is and receives only ‘Look on the field ridge.’ The records deploy the named wiping-tool in questions, predicates, answers, case titles, and commentary; they assign it no further stable gloss, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: Compound/object control follows the guide’s calibration: dry + excrement + stick names the latrine wiping-tool, while the corpus does not warrant claims about a particular material construction or a menu of symbolic readings. Seven exact witnesses from seven distinct works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 無位真人是甚麼乾屎橛？便歸方丈。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Joint Lamp Record (聯燈會要): Linji Yixuan asks what dry shit-stick the person of no rank is and returns to his quarters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 釋迦老子是乾屎橛。文殊普賢是擔屎漢。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元): Deshan Xuanjian calls old Shakyamuni a dry shit-stick and Manjushri and Samantabhadra dung-carriers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 覓什麼乾屎橛咬。以拄杖一時趁下。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extended Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen (雲門匡真禪師廣錄): Yunmen Wenyan asks what dry shit-stick the assembly seeks to chew and drives them down with his staff.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲門因僧問。如何是佛。門云乾屎橛。無門曰。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Gateless Barrier (無門關): Yunmen Wenyan is the quoted answerer who says “dry shit-stick”; Wumen Huikai records the case and begins his separate comment.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲門乾屎橛。頌云。雲門乾屎橛。全超法報化。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao names Yunmen’s dry shit-stick as the case and repeats it at the opening of his verse.

Occurrences.Kwic: 庭前栢樹子麻三斤乾屎橛之類。略無義路與人穿鑿。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Tianmu Zhongfeng (天目中峰廣錄): Zhongfeng Mingben lists the courtyard cypress, three catties of hemp, and dry shit-stick as sayings without a route of explanatory meaning to bore through.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The source’s continuing question sequence identifies Wanpu Zhao as the lay questioner; 師云 introduces Miyun Yuanwu’s separate reply.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyun (密雲禪師語錄): Wanpu Zhao asks Miyun Yuanwu what the dry shit-stick is; this occurrence preserves only Wanpu Zhao’s headword-bearing question.
